entry.title: LizstarTrek - Starfleet Acadamy Season 1 episodes 1 - 4
entry.content:
Every Sunday my Twitch subs and I watch Star Trek in my Discord. Here are my reviews and thoughts on each of the episodes as I see it. If you’re curious about a nerd’s views on Star Trek episodes, please read on, I go quite in depth with some of these episodes! I’ve watched some Star Trek before but not all of it!

Finally done with Discovery, thank god. It’s time for the newest show of the whole lot, as of this writing, we’re almost FINALLY caught up. Despite this being directly after Discovery and tying into it in many ways, I’ve heard good things about it. So let’s be optimistic.

Though we did some research into pre-production and Kurtzman kept saying this was “the hip and cool Trek for the youths” and holy shit, dude, could you be any more Old Man?

Kids These Days - DIS 7.5/10

We’re introduced to a small kid, Caleb Mir, who’s in a waiting cell with his Mom, who’s saying a whole lot of things that are saying “I am not going to be here for long”. She also gives him a weird creepy toy.

Apparently the two of them were working with a pirate, named Paul Giamatti. Wait shit, I’m sorry, his name is Paul Giamatti. Fuck, I mean- Anyways, Paul Giamatti really REALLY wanted to play a Klingon villain, and you can tell, he’s having the time of his life. He’s sent to prison, and Caleb’s mom is sent too for being an accomplice. Caleb then plays them for fools with the “I’m a little innocent kid~” shtick and breaks out of jail. This guy is gonna be our prococious scamp for the series who will have to learn the true meaning of friendship.

We then jump 15 years later. He’s a prisoner again. Damn, dude, can’t catch a break huh? He breaks free then is captured again. Maybe quit while you’re ahead.

We meet this lady, Nahla Ake, a half Human half Lanthanite. She was the captain who split up Caleb and his mom and lost him 15 years ago. She resigned over it cause she’s like “what I was told to do what fucked up and I refuse to have anything to do with it.” Admiral Sexypants from Discovery is like “hey we know where he is, maybe come out of retirement”. So she does, she goes to pick Caleb up and gets him to sign a deal saying “do community service with me at Starfleet Acadamy, and I help you find your mom, who btw broke out of jail a year ago and hasn’t even tried looking for you? That’s fucked up”

PRetty good character motivations so far. Discovery also started with a criminal who has to be forced into servitude to help the Federation, but uh, Caleb is a kid? He’s not an XO who makes dumb angry decisions for no reason. He’s a KID who makes dumb decisons for no reason! I can get behind that way better.

We get lots of shotgunning jokes and scenes introducing the rest of the cast. Lura Thok, a Jem Hadar/Klingon hybrid who’s a hardcore “YES SIR, STAND UP SOLDIER” type. “LET ME SEE YOUR WAR FACE!” Jay-Den, a Klingon cadet who’s signed up for medical stuff because he wants to “live a valiant life”. He also apologizes, which is a weird thing for a Klingon. I think I like his vibe already. Then of course, ya boi, the Doctor. I’m just happy to see him tbh. Also this Starfleet acadamy class takes place in a space ship that looks like the fucking Halo laser sword, and Ake sits in her chair in the most bisexual way I have ever seen.

Also, that’s three hybrid characters so far I think?? Ake, Thok, and and Paul Giamatti are all hybrid peoples. That’s rad tbh. More of that, please. This shit is a melting pot, let that pot MELT. No wonder this series pissed off fascists.

We get a scene of some rich kid bullying the Klingon for some fucking reason while everyone is like “WHAT ARE YOU DOING WHY ARE YOU DOING THAT” but only Caleb actually stands up for him and gets him his binoculars back. Jay-Den likes to go bird watching. I legit love this guy already??? He’s basically a Klingon I would write.

We also meet two other kids. Genesis, a kind of haughty but friendly girl, and SAM, a hologram. Or, as she prefers, “photonic”. Ohhh, Genesis is actually kind of a FREAK. “I want to learn how to kill a man with a toothbrush”. Caleb legit reacts by going “What the FUCK?” They’re also ALREADY teasing a romance between these two. That was fast.

The ship flies into a place that immediately tries to blow it up. Why the fuck are we doing that??? This ship has kids on it. What is it, the Enterprise? A big spiky obviously evil ship is blowing them the fuck up. The cadets all gotta step up once Lura gets stabbed by some debris. Caleb knows a way to stop this, and starts to work with it. We also learn who the villain here is. It’s Nus Braka, AKA Paul Giamatti! He’s fun. Apparently Giamatti’s favorite Trek is DS9 and you can tell cause he wants to be Gul Dukat. But like, a little less of a “convinces himself he’s the good guy” and leaning a bit more into the “Gul Dukat was a weird creepy pervert”. We also learn the reason he knows they’re here is cause Caleb is trying to send messages to his mom. Everyone blames him but like, I dunno dog, he was just trying to send messages to his mom.

All of the cadets get time to shine here. Even the rich pretty boy, Darem, shines. He’s “Khaonian”, which allows him to um… Mystique himself and live in space. He’s blue now, that’s his attack. Oh they’re also pushing stuff with him and Genesis. Time for a loooove trongle! Anyways Darem then almost freezes to death. I mean, that’s not how heat works in space, he wouldn’t radiate all that that fast, but that’s okay. Genesis ends up saving him using a tractor beam.

There’s actually some really good jokes here. A lot of them from Thok. “IF I AM GOING TO DIE TODAY, I NEED LESS CHEERFULNESS”. And when she gives a friendly shoulder punch to Jay-Den, he just goes flyyyiiiing. Also I like Caleb’s sass.

Caleb manages to do his thing and they blow up Giamatti’s ship. He escapes in an escape pod, laughing maniacally as he does.

We then get a weird slowmo flyby of each of the characters as a weird slow version of “If You’re Going To San Fransisco” plays. I’ve never been a huge fan of this kinda thing.

Captain Ake gives Caleb the chance to just… dip. He stays with them for 90 days and 100 hours of labor to pay off his jail time, and she helps him find his mom. OR he just leaves. He of course decides to stay, because she show has to happen.

I actually liked that. Honestly pretty up there for a first episode for a Trek series.

Beta Test - DIS 7.5/10

Everyone makes it to Starfleet Acadamy, the first class on campus in like 100 years cause y’know, Burn shenanigans. Also we get the intro for the first time. It looks like a cutscene from Civilization 4 that should have “Baba Yetu” playing over it.

Caleb and the pretty boy are roommates. Neither are happy about this.

EXOCOMP!!! There’s also a Brikar, Rak-Tahk’s species, that’s sick as hell.

This was the only thing I knew about this character. That she goes barefoot. Also that she sits in a bisexual manner. Anyways she’s talking with Admiral Sexpot and some other Federation bigwig who is immediatley unlikable. They’re trying to get Betazoid to rejoin the Federation. JETT RENO IS HERE!! I STILL LOVE HER. This is actually the most dialogue they ever gave her like… ever. She always showed up like every three episodes in Discovery to say two lines that were the best lines of the episode.

Apparently BDG was in this episode. He voiced a DOT that says “hello”. Jeremy Coulhain was the other one. That’s fucking wild. Also the school chime is the Trek theme, which means the Trek theme exists in the world of Trek. Who wrote the in universe Trek theme?

Caleb makes an ass out of himself in front of the princess of Betazed, basically. She teases the hell out of him in a “I am clearly into you but I’mma play with your emotions cause I know what they are~” kinda way. It’s a little cute, ngl. She tells the people in charge she wants him to be her guide around the campus. Everyone is like “HIM??????”

They connect in a nice way. He’s an awkward guy who can’t trust anyone due to his shitty-ass life. They go to Cetacean Ops for a date. Are they allowed to do that??? That’s Yuri appropriation. Also this is the first time we see Cetacean Ops in live action!!! Things kinda go south when the other Betazeds can’t contact her in Cetacean Ops, and they get in trouble. Well, Caleb gets in trouble. HE WAS DOING WHAT SHE WANTED?? SHE ASKED FOR IT? Also she gives him government secrets, showing her that the planet his mother is apparently on is behind the Betazed Psychic Wall.

Oh also I may have to mention, the Betazed leader speaks in sign language. I can’t believe Star Trek is woke now. Hey anyways I was thinking about one of my favorite TNG season 2 episodes recently, Loud As a Whisper, which had a mute actor as one of the main characters?

Anyways, the princess finds out Caleb is kinda using her to find his mom and won’t open up to her about why, and reacts poorly. The Betazed leader walks out of the negatiations partly because of this. And then we get a THIRD SCENE of Ake trying to convince Caleb not to leave. Hopefully this isn’t a thing that happens every episode.

Caleb opens up to the princess, being honest to someone else for once maybe since he was like, 4. He explains WHY he used her, and tries to convince her to help this move along. She does, and Betazed rejoins.

The princess joins… the War College. lol. But hey, her brother is now Caleb’s new roommate! He’s very awkward.

I do like all these episode so far, I think my #1 problem is they’re too long. Every episode is like an hour and 15 minutes.

Vitus Reflux - DIS 7.5/10

We get some stuff about the War College VS Starfleet. The War College cadets are…. weird assholes? And they start pranking the Starfleet Cadets for no reason. They hack the teleporters to drag them out of the locker room and into random spots on campus. And then brag about it over intercoms going “We do this cause we can. And cause it’s fun”. Um, expel them??

Also, Darem is bisexual and polyamarous. Holy shit. Are we going to get a polyam love triangle????

Thok tries to convince Ake to just… use authority to stop this. But she’s like “this is kid shit, and I’m for kid shit”. lol she’s a weirdo. She basically helps them get even, with some botony thing.

Meanwhile, Genesis signs Caleb up for a sports thing. He has NO interest, but she’s an admiral’s daughter and HAS to be leader, and has to win. To an unhealthy degree. And he’s the most obviously competent one there, except for maybe Jay-Den.

The sport is just laser tag! If Laser Tag was the Battle at Normandy. It’s so fucking funny the idea that they replaced Parrises Squares with a full phaser battle charge because it’s safer than Parrises Squares ever was. That’s so funny.

All of the characters are having moments where they talk and sass each other and oh my GOD imagine characters like, just having character moments and interracting in normal regular moments. Then you can have things stand out better when shit hits the fan! Instead of just like… having them only ever talk to each other when serious shit is going down.

Caleb talks to the Betazed Princess, who’s name is actually Tarima, I guess I need to name her since she’s around more often. She seems pretty distant about all of this. Who knows where this is going tbh

Darem wins captaincy of the sports team because he got Genesis mad my mocking her. Rude. At least he gets his comeuppance by having the war college people prank him again, but honestly it’s mostly aimed at them mocking poor Sam. Darem decides they’re going to do a sports match after hours to get back at them. They are very much outmatched and not gonna win. Genesis steps out of this because A) “A true captain doesn’t send their team into a slaughter” and B) “They don’t do underhanded shit like you did to win”. She’s 100% right. But then she shows up anyway cause I mean this guy is totally gonna whiz it down his leg.

Darem does in fact continually suck ass and his stretegies keep fucking them over. Genesis actually comes up with ideas and strategies and uses her training to win. Darem ends up quitting over this, but the game is ended anyways when the teachers find out about it and break it up. Everyone gets in massive trouble. Except Darem I guess. They react to this by uh…. trying to prank the war college even harder.

HOLY SHIT JETT RENO AND THOK ARE DATING?! Also Reno is 100% the top.

Darem says his mommy and daddy issues are the reasons he’s an asshole. They forgive him, but hope that he can be better.

The rest of the episode is a heist. Well, until this happens

Tarima aplogizes for being weird, buuuuut they’re still not super on the same terms. But she DOES kiss him! Oh, kids.

Anyways the prank goes without a hitch. And what ws the prank? Exactly the shit Ake had planned up and th ought of, cause she’s a pranking genius, and she kept feeding it to them through Code. That’s fun.

I liked this one too, but it was leaning a bit into the fratboy college stuff in a way that didn’t resonate with me, but it’s not BAD, just not super my thing. I do like when it all comes back to “Starfleet is good and all about empathy and working together for a better tomorrow” and that’s the main takeaway though.

Vox In Excelso - DIS 6.5/10

The Doctor is teaching debate. Jay-Den is NOT happy about this, he does not like public speaking. They do like, a tournament of debate. Caleb wins every single debate, hardcore. He’s actually very good at debate. When it gets to Jay-Den, he just… has a panic attack. Poor Jay-Den.

I REALLY like Caleb and Jay-Den’s friendship.

We also learn some Klingon lore. There were basically no Klingons in Discovery post time skip, so we learn a few things. The Burn caused Qo’noS to become uninhabitable and now Klingons are nearing extinction. That’s… that’s fucking nuts. What the fuck? They’re showing this off through a flashback montage. What the fuck is it with Modern Star Trek and blowing up the capital planets of the other major forces? This is the first major worldbuilding mistep of all of this. And y’all KNOW how I love my Klingons, so…

Anyways we learn that Jay-Den’s family might have died. And we get some flashbacks to him on a refugee planet. He was close with his brother, who supported him in what he wanted to do, but his dad didn’t understand and wanted him to be a warrior like the rest of them. But his brother is cool as hell. “Your mind is hungry, brother. We must feed it!” He wants to get his bro some Federation tech.

We’ve got two major plots. One, the debate team is basically debating the rights of the Klingons to… exist? And that they should be helped to survive? Not sure what’s going on there. Notably, Jay-Den is anti-Federation help. And Ake is going to try and talk to some Klingon leaders to offer them aid and help.

More flashbacks. Jay-Den’s brother is killed trying to trade for Federation technology. Jay-Den is not allowed to try and save him because of his parents’ bigotry.

Ake meets up with an old… “friend”. They were ABSOLUTELY fucking. They get smmmaaaashed. Okay yes, later on in a later scene, they were 100% fucking and it almost went somewhere but they were both too married to their jobs and cultures. A shame. They’re cute together.

Of ALL the people to help psych up and therapy Jay-Den, it’s Darem. Also it’s very, VERY gay.

It’s now the day of the debate. Ake is hung over. It doesn’t go well. Caleb VS Jay-Den ends with them yelling at each other Thok is like “Well I’ve never been an advisor for another Klingon and I don’t wanna fuck it up but I’ll do my best.” She rights his views on his family and is like “They didn’t abandon you, they let you go so you can be here in the only way they could”. It’s pretty nice.

Jay-Den goes back up to the debate stage so he can give a big debate about why the Federation shouldn’t just give the Klingons what they need, and force them to stop being Klingons. It’s a good scene, though I dunno why they have so many bright lights in my face. He ends up giving a new idea. “We should solve a Klingon problem with a Klingon solution.”

What’s that solution? Go to war with the Klingons. It’s all one big excuse to let the Klingons win the planet as spoils of war. Also frankly it’s foreplay for Ake and her klingon boytoy.

The episode is good. I do not like the stupid lore stuff with the Klingons but the writing and how they handled it in this episode were good. I just… man I wish we didn’t have to deal with the Burn still, and all the nonsense that came with it.

We cut it to four episodes tonight cause holy SHIT why are these episodes an hour and 20 minutes?????

entry.title: LizstarTrek - Discovery Season 5 episodes 6 - 10
entry.content:
Every Sunday my Twitch subs and I watch Star Trek in my Discord. Here are my reviews and thoughts on each of the episodes as I see it. If you’re curious about a nerd’s views on Star Trek episodes, please read on, I go quite in depth with some of these episodes! I’ve watched some Star Trek before but not all of it!

I know literally nothing about Discovery, except for The Burn, and that it leads into Strange New Worlds. So uh… I’ve been dreading this one. But hey, who knows! Maybe it’ll surprise me!!

It has not so far. Y’all ready to see Michael save the universe again??? ….I am so insanely checked out of this it’s not even funny.

Whistlespeak - DIS 3/10

This looks like a 1999 point and click adventure game background

Anyways, they are having trouble figuring out the next clue. Michael gets snippy and insubordinate with Cronenberg. Meanwhile, Dr. Culber invents using the brain scans of dead loved ones to create holograms for therapy sessions. DR. CULBER INVENTED DEAD PEOPLE LLMS FOR THERAPY. I HATE THIS.

“Maybe try scanning every culture in the database for ones that put an emphasis on the importance of water” YOU MEAN ALL OF THEM?

They finally find a culture that seems to fit their clue so they go down to a planet with sme people who speak in “Whistlespeak”, a long range form of vocalation. That’s kinda neat, I guess. Tilly and Michael beam down because Michael will be cold in the fucking grave before anyone does anything without her.

They meet up with some natives, one of whom appears sick. They are taken to a group who minister treatment, which is loud noise that overwhelms Michael and knocks her on her ass. They do become friends with the group though, and basically join in some race to meet the gods or something. I dunno, this is kinda cool. It’s a dangerous run though, I like non-offensive native cultures. Also Michael drops out of the race, so it’s up to Tilly to possibly win, which means maybe Tilly will get to do a thing!

Hot man alert. Say the line, Liz.

Tilly ends up befriending one of the other racers and helps her to cross the finish line. It’s cute, and a good moment. Aaaand then it turns out those who win the race will be killed to help “bring the rain” and “meet the gods”. Oh boy.

Meanwhile, back on Discovery, Adira is having a lot of anxiety cause they’re put on the bridge on an important mission and y’know, that shit’s scary. Poor Adira.

Tilly and her friend are locked in a big stone tower. Discovery can’t get a lock on them. Dude. Anyways Michael breaks the prime directive to get them to open the door. Just fucking whizzing that prime directive. She has NO qualms about this, it’s just bam, prime directive shattered. She fucking teleports in front of this guy.

“Are you a god?” “Yes” MICHAEL. DO YOU KNOW WHAT THE PRIME DIRECTIVE IS AND WHY IT EXISTS?

WHY ARE YOU A STARFLEET CAPTAIN.

Who Watches the Watchers this is not…. But WHY do I dislike this so much compared to that episode? Cause it’s kinda similar. Is it just cause I’m so checked out? Cause I hate Michael so much?

Neli suggests it’s cause in Who Watches the Watchers, it’s Picard teaches them “well there are others, and we’re all just people, that’s fine, we all bleed”, where-as here it’s Michael going “you’re all primatives who can’t understand the real way the world works. Maybe eventually you won’t kill yourselves for no reason, idiots”.

Anyways they get the thing and go home whatever.

Erigah - DIS 1.5/10

The Federation captures Moll and L’ak and bring them into custody. Nhan is here again. Remember her? She’s uh, she’s here now again! Man they just write people out with tearful goodbyes then bring them back CONSTANTLY. If someone doesn’t fucking die, a goodbye means nothing.

She gets pissy at Book and he’s like “Come on man that was last season. I’m better now.” “YOU SET OFF A WEAPON THAT BROKE SPACETIME.” “Pobody’s nerfect!”

Someone sent the “Eto, bleh~” gif from that one anime and it broke chat for a minute after this.

Anyways the Breen find out they have two fugitives and are like “GIVE NOW”. They just… decide to ignore that for now, claiming that Discovery is too busy to bring them the fugitives right now.

We also learn more about the Breen. It’s uh… a little rough! “Genocide is their version of the prime directive”. What the hell dude. Also lots of DS9 references cause I mean, they’re a DS9 centric race. Apparently they haven’t been interracted with SINCE the Dominion War? They’re not THAT far away, y’all, it’s been like 700 years.

When the Breen DO show up, they try to slow them down with legislation. It doesn’t really work, they have one hour to comply or it’ll be an act of war. That thing up there is the Breen ship btw. Remember when we saw the giant Romulan ship, the D’deridex for the first time and it dwarfs the Constitution? Or the Borg Cube and it’s even larger than that? Yeah uh, it’s getting old. Also I dunno why exactly the Breen have huge-ass ships like this. They sure didn’t in DS9.

We get some Tragic Backstory for Rayner. He hates the Breen because apparently they ruled over Kellerun for a while. A lot of this is giving me the energy of that one TNG episode with the Cardassians and O’Brien, but I know this won’t be NEARLY as good.

They try to bluff the Breen into accepting a deal with them. It almost works, but then it turns out the guards they set to watch L’ak are FUCKING BAD and he kills himself in his cell. The resulting battle between Moll and everyone is fucking painful to watch, it just sso much and the camera is FLAILING.

lmfao “IF ANY HARM FALLS TO L’AK BY THE FEDERATION, WAR IS INEVITABLE.” “We swear he will not be harmed.” “Hey uh, Burnham, it’s Laan, I have some news for you”. IT’S ALMOST COMEDIC.

I should still REALLY be liking Moll but I do not. She’s a rebel without a cause. She’s antagonistic because she refuses to not be, and she could EASILLY work with us instead.

Oh good, we’re making sure she’s COMPLETELY irradeemable! She sides with THE FUCKING BREEN and tells them about the super weapon and says she’ll tell them how to get to it. I mean, tbf, she wouldn’t actually be able to get to the weapon, she doesn’t fucking know where it is and is like 3 clues behind.

God I cannot care about this. I guess at least we’re not at war.

Labyrinths - DIS 2/10

We are so annoyed with having to watch this that we are now watching at 125% speed. These episodes feel like they are a million years long.

Anyways, Moll is now allied with the Breen and says she’ll use the Progenitor’s weapon to bring L’ak back to life. YOU DON’T EVEN REALLY KNOW WHAT THE PROGENITOR’S THING DOES, NO ONE HAS SEEN IT IN 800 YEARS.

Meanwhile, Discovery makes it to the Badlands, which is apparently where the next clue is kept. Remember the Badlands from DS9? This is the successor season for DS9! I hate my life!

They’re visiting a library that’s just sitting in the middle of the Badlands. They have to fly through the Badlands, which in DS9 was dangerous but here it just almost makes Discovery explode. They have a library card that allows them to like, check out this weapon or whatever. Dude, I dunno.

I used to be a library. I should like big science fiction star trek library. It’s a giant tower of books, I built a place like this in Dwarf Fortress once. The archivists show them to a chamber linked to the library card, which just… has a book sitting in it. It’s just been there forever.

“It’s fun to have a book visit the library for a change!” the archivist says to Booker. That’s cute. She gives him a cutting of the Kweijan world tree, which he almsot cries at.

Michael touches a thing in the book and is locked in her own mind in a test. Everyone else now has to sit there and watch her lay on the ground knocked out. “Oh by the way if you fail this mission you will die. Sorry.” Wh-why? Why would they build it like this? “The creator of this wants you to succeed” SURE DOESN’T SEEM LIKE IT.

The Breen can track discovery for some reason, so they now know where they are. The Library tells them to go the fuck away. This archive should have some dangerous guns on it tbh, they should be able to handle a Breen ship. But of course the Breen have to be super impossible to overcome.

Oh come on Michael. We don’t love you now.

“Me being too focused on my job is why I lost Book.” Um, no. You lost Book because he tried really hard to do genocide. I know, those two things are easy to mix up.

All her weird therapy session about her fears of death and her workaholic personality would be good, if it wasn’t all the correct thing for her to do at all points because she’s always been right always and is the perfect special boy. Anyways it turns out this is the correct thing, because “to handle what the progenitors left behind, you must be able to express your emotions like fear, guilt, and doubt”. SHE’S LITERALLY NEVER EXPRESSED THOSE IN ANY OTHER EPISODE OF THIS SERIES :D

Anyways they succeed in getting the thing and leave and the Breen just start attacking it. They demand that Michael hand over the map they got or they’ll destroy the archive. So Michael hands it over if they swear a blood oath, though she sets up a trick in case they blow her up to get away and pretend she’s been killed. They blow her up, and then decide to kill it anyways cause ha ha, they’re evil! Moll ends up just… killing the Breen leader instead. And all the Breen for some reason isntantly join under her banner.

I guess I liked the library in this one.

Lagrange Point - DIS 2/10

Hey, thats a fun Famicom game.

They gotta get to where the Precursor weapon is before the Breen do. Now that the previous Breen leader is dead lots of other Breen leaders are heading there to try and take his ship and soldiers under their banners. So now Discovery has to get there as soon as they can. They show up to two black holes and find a case floating in the lagrange point between them. Then the Breen instantly show up and just park right next to the black holes, because that ship is invincible until we need to blow it up later this season.

Moll nabs the progenitor’s box, and we need to steal that back, so Michael and gang sneak on board pretending to be Breen. This place is so fucking green. Waht is this, the Borg?

Michael has to do some fiddling while Book distracts a Breen guard. Book flirts with him. It’s actually a little funny. It took 5 seasons but we finally found banter that kind of works. Book just pulling out the Kris Special and flirting with someone he knows nothing about, and it somehow landing. “I will make a space for you in the oil bath” “Yo Michael hurry up this is getting weird”.

Saru has to go risk his life. He and his girlfriend hug. Hey, come on. Kira kissed Odo’s makeup-covered face and smeared it all over herself, go ham on this guy!

The sneaking plan fails so Discovery takes on this giant Breen ship and blows it up easily. ….Told you. Michael and Moll dive into the Precursor tech and disappear to who knows where.

Life, Itself - DIS 2/10

Here we are. The payoff. Everything we’ve ever worked towards is here at last. Also once again, important to note that all of this came about because they watched an okay episode of TNG and completely misunderstood the point of it.

Anyways Michael is in some weird dimension. She’s thrown around after touching some shit and lands in a rainy space. There are ALSO Breen in this space, and when they show up they just try to kill her for no reason. When Michael finally meets up with Moll, turns out the Breen are attacking her now too. Why? Wh-why???? She’s their leader last they knew. Moll and Michael team up.

Nevermind, Michael immediately turns on her and kicks her legs out. And then instead of stealing her gun, runs away????? We then get a VERY CGI fight scene.

Meanwhile on the Discovery, we get the conclusion to the Culber and Stamets storyline. Culber goes on a suicide mission so he can finish “trying to find what he’s looking for”, whatever that means. Culber and Stamets deserved better.

Michael and Moll team up…. AGAIN. “STAND DOWN, MOLL!” You’re the one that kicked her!!! Michael then solves the puzzle and techno babbles her way through the maze.

Moll betrays Michael this time. She listens to Michael to how to use the machine, then knocks her out and tries to revive her husband. She fails because she wasn’t listening and sets up the machine improperly. She has literally spent this entire season just ignoring everyone who’s trying to talk to her and help her. So, y’know, it fits. I do not like this character.

Saru comes back to be cool one last time and convince the Breen reinforcements to turn around and leave by having the best poker face. Well, at least Saru is still cool.

Michael wakes up, and fixes Moll’s stupid nonsense, solving the puzzle by herself and activating the mechanism properly. She then meets a Progenitor. I’d like to think the Progenitors are all women since we’re only met two. She’s like “Hi, I am a brain recording here to tell you how to operate this technology without killing anyone.”. She also says 2 things: 1) It can make a genetic clone but they have none of the personality of memories. We already have that, it’s called cloning. Then 2) The Progenitors did not actually make this technology, they just found it, and assume whoever made it made them. omfg.

If this wasn’t already a franchise with MULTIPLE godlike being established, this MIGHT be meaningful!

We get a 2001 Space Odyssey scene, with Michael deciding not to use the Life Device after seeing like, God or whatever. I honestly dunno. I don’t understand 2001, and that’s GOOD. Anyways, she goes back to Discovery, everything is calm and good now, and she’s like “We need to blow that thing up.” “But our orders are to bring it back for the Federation!” “Yeah well, they’ve always let me do whatever I want before with no reprucussions so this’ll be fine too.” “Makes sense to me.”

Moll is incarcerated, but Book is like “it should be fine, we can make sure you get a fair trial”. Ha ha, a LOT of people died because of her. Cronenberg is like “We’ll turn her into a secret agent it’s fine.”

SPEAKING of Cronenberg, we find out he’s under a codename. His real name is… Agent Daniels. YES. FOR REAL. THIS IS SO SLOPPILY REVEALED.

Saru gets married, which is cute. Still no kiss. Tilly decides she’s gonna start a mentorship program at Starfleet Acadamy. YOU DIDN’T HAVE ONE OF THOSE?! Aaaand Book and Michael get back together. Come on, he’s been doing SO MUCH BETTER after the whole genocide terrorism fiasco.

We then jump ahead into the future and see Old Michael. We then get a BIG extra long scene of Michael, Book, and their son. They live in a magical red forest with a magical deer neighbor. I love that deer tbh. And honestly I’d live in this house in a heartbeat. This is like, almost a magical christmas commercial… Finally, some real Raktajino.

Michael is an Admiral! We won’t see her get to that point, but she got there I guess. She and her son go and see The Discovery, which is being re-named “The Discovery A”. Why is this still going? She’s here to send the ship, and Zora, to the edge of space and have her sit there alone for as long as something will happen.

Why does this happen? So Calypso, the Short Trek episode, could happen. Yes. They really cared THIS HARD to make that accurate, and retconned it to make it happen in the 43rd century. So now to fix this they have Zora, completely sapient, just being sent to sit around for a thousand years for a reason they will never explain. We’ve already established that Zora is a life form. Why are we doing this? Also the future seen in Calypso is kinda dark and sucks. This blows.

Then we get scenes of the rest of the crew coming on board, and they’re all young again, so uh, it’s the end of the Titanic.

Off the Discovery goes, to the middle of nowhere. Goodbye. Maybe this is the fate it deserves.

….

……..

I hated this entire show and will never watch it again as long as I live. There was maybe one episode that’s a standout and that’s it. God damn.

entry.title: LizstarTrek - Discovery Season 5 episodes 1 - 5
entry.content:
Every Sunday my Twitch subs and I watch Star Trek in my Discord. Here are my reviews and thoughts on each of the episodes as I see it. If you’re curious about a nerd’s views on Star Trek episodes, please read on, I go quite in depth with some of these episodes! I’ve watched some Star Trek before but not all of it!

I know literally nothing about Discovery, except for The Burn, and that it leads into Strange New Worlds. So uh… I’ve been dreading this one. But hey, who knows! Maybe it’ll surprise me!!

It has not so far. Y’all ready to see Michael save the universe again??? ….I am so insanely checked out of this it’s not even funny.

Red Directive - DIS 1.5/10

God, okay, let’s do more of this shit then.

Everyone is like “Wow life is so boring now that things have calmed down”. WE WERE ALMOST IN AN APOCALYPTIC SCENARIO, GET YOUR HANDS OUT OF YOUR PANTS, Y’ALL. Luckily the big wigs show up to tell Michael they have a job for her to do, and she seems almost giddy they’re doing a “red directive”, some kind of super secret dangerous mission. Then she announces it to the whole crew.

Fire this woman.

Also Kronenberg is here again. He’s kind of taking on the role of what I’d call “The Star Trek G-Man”.

Meanwhile, BREEN! REMEMBER THEM? We see a Breen for the first time ever without the helmet on, and he looks like this.

The Breen wear the helmets because they are made of Goo, and in non cold environments, they turn liquidy.

Goo Girls in Star Trek, confirmed.

This Breen and some Human, I think, are on this Romulan ship the Disco crew is trying to salvage. The Disco crew coems in guns blazing in a breach and clear situation like they’re marines. I miss TNG. Riker would do this away mission better.

Oh my GOD, HOLD THE FUCKING CAMERA STEADY, WHAT IS WRONG WITH YOU.

They get into a fight with the Breen and his hot goth wife. Michael gets spaced and for some reason her suit materializes a space suit. WHY DOESN’T IT DO THAT FOR EVERYONE?!

Some ship shows up to help them, and they merge their warp bubbles. “We can’t beam you because the merged warp bubbles are messing with it” DO YOU KNOW LITERALLY ANYTHING ABOUT STAR TREK? They fall out of warp while she’s out in her suit. She should have become a fucking red paste in that space suit.

They randomly pick up Book. He’s here now!

I want to make it clear, I am directly explaining what happens. They just go and get Book, and Michael acts confused about it. Girl, it’s YOUR MISSION.

Oh shit, they’re also bringing Tilly back. Y’all, why do you write anyone out of this show if you’re just gonna awkwardly bring them the fuck back? Anyways she’s wasted, hits on some guy (so you know she’s straight), and then talks to Michael over the phone.

Meanwhile the Breen and his hot wife go to deliver their stolen goods tosome black market dealer, who’s a Data-style android. He’s weird and creepy. His name is Fred. He tries to rip them off and they fight their way out. I can’t tell if they’re good guys or bad guys. They are at least very in love? They’re very protective of each other, maybe it’s a Bonnie and Clyde type thing. Anyways the Federation shows up and downloads data from Fred’s brain so they can follow the scavengers. Why is this episode still going on?

Back at Federation Base Camp they find out whatever it is they stole is some kind of massive galactic threat. Fucking CHRIST, y’all, you just CAN’T HELP YOURSELVES, CAN YOU? Just one season, JUST ONE SEASON, IT’S ALL I FUCKING ASK.

We get a giant bike chase. In response, the scavengers cause an avalanche that will threaten to kill thousands, but the two ships crash themselves and use their shields to stop the avalanche of sand. Big exciting, whoo. For some reason the scavengers stayed until the VERY END and then leave. Did they just…. want to see if they killed people??

We finally find out wtf this is all about. One of the things they stole was a diary that might give clues to the wereabouts to the last notes by an ancient Romulan scientist, Vellek. You might remember that name, he’s from the episode where they meet an alien who’s the progenitor of all humanoid life in the galaxy. Vellek seems to have discovered a way to create life like the Progenitors did. I… didn’t THINK that was what that episode was about. They didn’t CREATE all life, all humanoid life is descended from them. So, now they’re taking these aliens and turning them into like, godlike precursor beings. WE ALREADY HAVE PLENTY OF THOSE.

The point of The Chase was “We are all the same”, not “GODS EXIST AND THEY CREATED US”. Just use the fucking Iconians if you want a super precursor civilation, they’re right there. Or bring back the Slavers, honestly that would blow my fucking mind.

Under the Twin Moons - DIS 2.5/10

They THINK they might know where this Romulan scientist’s last stuff is, so they go to an ancient uninhabited planet to find it. This is also Saru’s final mission, as he will be retiring, so as they go down, he and Michael talk about who’s gonna be the new XO. Tilly still doesn’t want to be here. So who?

It’s Book. It’s obviously Book.

DO NOT MAKE YOUR SIGNIFICANT OTHER YOUR XO.

Some ancient security system pops up and tries to kill them. That captain from the last episode shows up to help, and tells them how to fix it. I don’t like him, he’s arrogant and rude. I’m skipping over stuff cause it’s just action to fill space.

“I was searching through Dark Comms”, says Booker, like that’s a normal thing. Did they seriously invent The Dark Web but for Star Trek? He tries to message them to just talk this through, and he SEEMS to recognize Moll, the girl. She’s the daughter of his old mentor. Oh boy, connections! Is Moll short for Molly? What a coincidence, good thing space isn’t that big.

They get to whatever it is they’re looking for and it points them in the direction of Trill.

We get another tearful goodbye to Saru. I think this is the third time we’ve done this. And who is the new XO gonna be?

Why does he look like an American Daniel Craig. She’s like “I have the upmost belief in you”. But I already know as soon as he says anything counter to her it’s gonna be angst city.

Jinaal - DIS 2/10

The new XO’s name is Rayner. He’s awkward. They demoted this fucking guy for this. Poor Rayner. He’s back down to Commander.

They need to go to Trill and talk to a Symbiont who is still alive and has knowledge of all of this, cause it was alive years ago. Its current host refuses to speak to anyone who doesn’t answer some fuck-ass riddle.

There’s also some kind of side plot with Saru helping his girlfriend out with ambassador work. Why do you keep writing Saru out of the show if you want to keep using him?

They put the Trill in Culber, and he’s immediately super suss and obviously evil. He puts them on a dangerous quest to make sure they are able to handle the thing they’re trying to find.

Why did they make Gray grow that heinous mullet? Adira and Gray’s relationship is on the rocks cause of long distance and they dunno how to make it work. No one who wrote this episode had been in a long distance relationship.

They for some reason are not treating Trill as the full settled civilized planet that it should be. Instead it’s…. Endor.

The Trill decides them worthy, because they didn’t just kill the animals that were attacking them.

Rayner is having problems cause no one really likes him that much. Have you considered not being weird? This episode feels weirdly elongated as well. Like the pacing is bad.

The episode ends with a stinger of “OH NO ONE OF THE PIRATES IS HERE TOO ON TRILL” just… chilling, and someone no one noticed the gothed up hot bitch in cult robes.

Face the Strange - DIS 4/10

We get some more character of the two scavengers/thieves/pirates/whatever. It’s L’ak and Moll. L’ak wants out of this and is uncomfy with all of it. Moll keeps killing people and is like “Just one more job babe and we’ll be out~” Also every single person in the underworld keeps trying to fuck them over so they keep having to kill people.

Hey remember how I called Michael getting pissy the SECOND her XO second guesses her? Well she does it. Why even have an XO, Michael? You’re always correct, you don’t need anyone telling you what to do. And you hate it when people do. It’s not like you need him for away missions, you send yourself on them instead.

While yelling at him, Stamets sees a weird bug melt, and then suddenly shit is bad. Everyone is passed out, they’re in a wormhole, and only Michael and Rayner are awake to stop it.

The ship is cycling through random time periods. For some reason Michael and Rayner are completely immune, because they… tried to teleport at the exact same time? Rayner says this is probably the work of a “Time Bug”, a Krenim weapon that you can rarely find on the black market, which makes ships randomly cycle through time periods for like, months. But Stamets is immune, as we know from the WORST FUCKING EPISODE EVER, because he lives outside of time.

They keep jumping between different periods in the show’s history and it kinda requires you to give a shit or remember any of it but I’ve been trying to purge this fucking show from my brain, because it’s a waste of my limited memory. This episode is literally just a super complicated high budget clip show.

“Okay now that we’re collected the things, you go do it, Michael” Um? No? Stamets, you’re the fucking engineer, YOU do it?

THey keep failing to kill this bug over and over. Just jumping around to things, which makes the previous stuff htey were doing moot. We get to see Michael fight herself from season 1. They make Season 1 Michael seem like a super angry bitter fucker. She wasn’t, she was just depressed and emotionless. It’s weird because they are retroactively making her super unstable but she’s always been correct about everything.

Michael has to connect with the crew to get them to trust her, so she tells them all about things she knows about them. This is also stuff we learn just now because none of them are characters. We also get to see Airam again, because of this.

It works, they only lose 6 hours, and they’re chasing after the baddies again.

Mirrors - DIS 3/10

They reach the next clue on the Davinci Code-ass jounrey they’re on, and it’s a big-ass wormhole in space. Why have we not explored this already? Wormholes are very important. I watched DS9, that’s like the whole fucking point of it. That, and Trills Are Hot And Fascists Suck Ass. Those are the only 3 things you should take away from DS9, yes.

Michael and Book need to go into the wormhole, where they find the mirror Enterprise stuck in interdimensional space. Meanwhile, Rayner is in charge of Discovery for the first time and he’s still kind of unlikable. Interesting A and B plot, totally not unfitting side by side.

Book and Michael explore the Enterprise. Michael is like “Oh this is where my brother was. Surely this will not end with her being proven wrong and being sad about it all.

They finally find Moll and L’ak and we learn why they’re doing this. They have a “Breen Blood Bounty” on them, we also learn L’ak is Breen, though I spoiled that immediately. Whoops.

Why did they remove the muzzles from the Breen helmets? Didn’t want Dog Goo People? That’s what this series was missing. If L’ak was a doggy goo girl, I’d give every episode a 10. Your loss, Discovery.

we then start jumping back and forth from the flashback to present. Weird, dunno why? This episode is very Clap Nerds, cause y’know, it expands on Breen Lore. The Breen were a part of late DS9, but we never got a LOT about them or their culture or their people. We literally never heard them speak a language we could understand. We learn that like…. they wear these suits to keep goo, otherwise they solidify, and it’s the Breen Way to be goo. Being solid is “inflexible and weak”. That’s why we wear these EXTREMELY inflexible suits. What’s the point in being goo if you’re goo in a fucking solid thing anyway?! That’s so dumb?!

We also learn that Book’s mentor, and Moll’s father was maybe not the person Book thought he was. Or, Moll has a very bad opinion of him, and he abandoned her. “Hey may have been a shit dad to you, but he was a great mentor to me.” Uh, not really the best line, Book.

Back in the present, they have a very tenuous truce. Which basically ends as soon as they do what they need to do, then it’s back to fighting. I mean, the two of them aren’t EVIL, they just are broken people who can’t trust anyone. It kinda just sucks.

THey manage to get out. Remember when they said earlier in the episode all life pods were launched already? I guess they fucking lied. The two scavengers just use it and run away…. Okay. Book and Michael escape in the Enterprise, and then send it back to HQ, telling Detmer and Owo to take it. So uh, did they just write Detmer and Owo out of the show? Goodbye to them, I guess. Remember when Owo was cool and they let her do something once? Never again.

entry.title: Retro Achievement Mastery 236 - La-Mulana
entry.content:
This is La-Mulana.

So, it’s March of 2026. And the Wii rollout happens. So many Wii and Wiiware games released for RA. I hadn’t been really doing much RA, but I rolled out of retirement to try and get the 50 so points needed to get the event badge (which I eventually did). But what would be the first game? There are so many good Wii games out there, and many more I’ve never played.

How about one I’ve played a hundred times that fucking hates you?

La-Mulana is a truly special game. Originally a free PC game from like, 2006, it was heavily inspired by hard as nails and convoluted MSX games. But it got a remake on the Wii in 2009. That remake is still available on Steam, in fact, and while it’s quite different from the original, it’s still very much worth it.

In La-Mulana you play as Lemeza, an archaeologist inspired by Indiana Jones who must enter the lost ruins of La-Mulana to try and find the Secret of Life. His father, Shawn, entered and never came back, so he must do what his father could not. Along the way you’ll scan tablets for hints and lore and fight enemies with your trusty whip and collect items and powerups and die and die and die and die

If La-Mulana is known for anything, it’s being very rude. I’ve beaten it a hundred times, so like, it’s nothing to me, I know every puzzle and combat situation like the back of my back. So, my stomach, which I can see. But for the uninitiated, it’s VERY hard to get into, and it is NOT for everyone. You have to like retro note taking puzzle games and appreciate it’s weird jank movement. Lemeza is pretty stiff and awkward to fight with, and some of these bosses are wild.

It is, at its heart, essentially just a metroidvania. But it takes that formula and twists it in such a way that honestly, I feel it’s part of a new genre. One that I’ve lovingly called “Galioustroids”. But usually people just call it like, Meta Puzzlers or Metroidvanias That Care About Information. As you progress you learn more and more lore and information that lets you do things you never would have thought. Games like this walked so Void Stranger or Tunic could soar.

That’s not to say it’s old or outdated. Absolutely not! Many of the puzzles are still fresh nonsense. They’d step up their game again in La-Mulana 2, I feel, which has some TRULY vile puzzles (the entirety of Hell is straight up fucked up), but this game is no slouch.

When this set came out, I was in a race to be the first person to master it, but sadly due to a mess up on my part (it’s hard to do the All Character Endings and I’d literally never done it before), I had to play the game three times so I was the third person to master it. But that’s fine. This won’t be the last time we see La-Mulana~

entry.title: Muppet Show Watch-along Season 2 Part 1
entry.content:
My friends and I are watching the Muppet Show on Wednesdays and I guess I’ll do a quick review and watchalong. But first, I guess we should talk about the thing about watching the Muppets in the year of our Luigi 2026.

The Muppet Show is a beloved institution, and everyone loves it. So you’d think it’d be super easy to watch today, right? It is NOT. It’s been re-released a bunch of times, but due to the nature of what the Muppet Show IS, the re-releases keep shifting and cutting things all over the place. So if you want the FULL experience, it’s pretty impossible. But you can do your best.

ANOTHER thing is, what is the order? If you ask Wikipedia, you get a specific answer. If you ask the Muppets wiki, you get another. We’re just… gonna do our best to watch them all in whatever order we can, alright? At least it’s obvious where the seasons begin and end.

And finally… the whole point of the Muppet Show is about the human guest stars who star alongside the Muppets. These are all the most famous stars of the 70s, so I know like, MAYBE five of them. Obviously, I’m gonna like an episode that stars Vincent Price, who I love, a little more than one that stars Sandy Duncan, who I do not know at all. There might be some jokes and commentary about those guest stars I just flat out do not get. I’m doing my best, but this isn’t like, a retrospective. This is a nerd who grew up watching random Muppets content who wants to watch the Muppets Show and the only way she can really connect to media is if she orders and ranks it all or some shit. So yeah, let’s do that.

Episode 201: Don Knotts 7/10

Our first season 2 episode, and hey, I know Don Knotts! Honestly, for a season 2 episode, it’s not THAT different from anything you’d see in season 1, no massive changes in design yet. Some muppets are now gone, that’s the main different for now.

The running joke is Fozzie plans part of the show, and gives the band a song they wanna play, so Floyd gives him some shades. He then wanders into stuff all day.

This one was alright. Don was really get up there in years, he looks like Lance Boyle.

Episode 202: Zero Mostel 7.5/10

I didn’t know who this guy was but when I said his name out loud my boyfriend went on a giant tirade about him and how he’s a fantastic Jewish actor. He seems cool at least!

The running joke here is it’s gonna be payday soon and Kermit needs like 25 bucks to pay the band. That’s like, 100 in today’s money. Damn, cheap band. The owner of the theater offers to spot them, if they put some entertainment back in the show, that entertainment being female wrestlers. Hell yeah! Sam does not take it well when he finds out. Sam has his normal head! :D

Zero does “What do the simple folk do” and it feels like it goes on for a million years. I do like the poem he does later, though!

FIRST BEAKER!!! THE BOY, HE IS HERE!

The story ends with Kermit finding a single lady wrestler but being unable to find another. When he offers it to Piggy she almost murders him. Ms. Piggy is seeming more herself here! She’s got a new puppet and says “moi” now! Anyways Kermit has to do it herself, I mean himself.

Episode 203: Milton Berle 7/10

Milton Berle was a very classic comic, even at the time. He’s fun, I like him trying to do a comedic monologue but getting heckled by The Boys. He doesn’t handle em well. If I’m being real, the Statler and Waldorf heckles are already better this season.

Our running plot is that Fozzie is afraid to talk to Berle, so he keeps trying to hide from him. Every other muppet treats him with basically no respect. Eventually Berle manages to coax him out of hiding and they do a big vaudville act.

First Pigs in Space segment! If we’re giving Ms Piggy top billing, we should give her MORE skits!

Episode 204: Rich Little 7/10

Rich Little’s thing appears to be impressions, which they lean on a lot. He opens up with impressions of W.C. Fields and Humphrey Bogart. I HAVE seen Casablanca, and uh, I mean, I guess it’s an okay impression? I feel I could do one of the same quality, I dunno. But then he does a bunch of impressions of Muppets and it’s loads of fun.

One of the best parts of moving past season 1 is Gonzo will become an actual character and not a background side character. I love Gonzo. Our running skit is that Gonzo is trying to do a dancing chickens act and it’s not going amazingly. They are, in fact, chickens. They use ACTUAL chickens here, not Henrietta.

The chicken he eventually gets up on stage is named Lolita. Not the name I’d choose for the chicken.

Episode 205: Judy Collins 5.5/10

We start this episode with Crazy Harry blowing up Judy Collins. Lots of Crazy Harry so far this season! They have her doing things like “I know an old lady who swallowed a fly” while feeder kink happens behind her. Feels like a waste of your Judy Collins. She later does “Send in the Clowns” which might be even more upsetting. What a weird song.

The running throughline here is that Scooter’s uncle is here. We finally get to meet him! He’s a piece of shit! He’s here to look at the theater so he can sell it to turn it into a junkyard, because “real junk is better than the junk you put in here!” This is eventually resolved just… cause. He decides not to cause it’ll just fall apart anyway.

Episode 206: Nancy Walker 6/10

Poor Kermit is sick today so Fozzie is taking over. He is Bad at this :) Poor Fozzie.

We get some fun gags out of this, like them accidentally doing At The Dance and Veterinary Hospital at the same time.

This doesn’t exactly take AWAY from Nancy Walker, but it does feel like they under use her.

At least she gets to suit and tophat dance iwth sweetums!

It’s all a long set up to a shaggy dog joke about how it’s Swine Flu. Ms Piggy is not happy.

Episode 207: Edgar Bergen 8.5/10

This is actually a two parter for guests, cause Edgar brought a bunch of his ventriliquist dummies, and they are of course treated as characters, being puppets. I know some people find them creepy, I like em. For some reason. Fozzy also tries to get into it, too! Keep your day job, Fozzie. Which is this.

Fozzie don’t got the sauce. This is actually the first time that the running skit is actually tied in to the guest, I think.

This is also the episode with the amazing cover of “Time in a Bottle”.

Episode 208: Steve Martin 9/10

The show starts with Kermit cancelling the show cause of a calendar snafu. Steve does not handle this well. As such, the entire premise is completely different. This is them putting on auditions for new acts. Fozzie is worried that he’ll be replaced.

Steve starts to audition as well. Just cause. He’s got an EXTREMELY chaotic energy, it’s fun to watch. He goes up three times to do random acts like balloon animals or juggling.

I also like Gonzo and his dancing cheese.

We end with Steve doing dueling banjos, and I like that song. This was a fun one.
